question: Can a distributional monotone gamut-fraction transport preserve AO6 style while remaining intrinsically bounded and avoiding the invalid CB26 paired affine slope?

operator.basis: deterministic orthonormal basis of the Rec.709 zero-luminance plane
operator.hue: one unweighted circular Procrustes rotation between valid CB11 and AO6 unit chroma directions
operator.gamut_fraction: chroma magnitude divided by exact maximum magnitude on the fixed-luminance RGB cube section
operator.fraction_transport: stable-rank empirical CB11 gamut fractions mapped to linearly interpolated AO6 empirical quantiles
operator.rank_rule: stable mergesort with midpoint ranks (rank+0.5)/N over valid CB11 pixels
operator.quantile_rule: linear interpolation over sorted valid AO6 fractions at midpoint ranks
operator.reconstruction: rotated CB11 hue and mapped AO6-distribution gamut fraction at exact CB11 luminance
operator.neutral_rule: CB11 chroma below 1e-12 remains exact neutral
operator.scale: unchanged analytical safe step only for source-boundary and float32 margin preservation
operator.forbidden: paired affine slope, 3D covariance, local map, robust weights, nonlinear fitted parameters, target dose, semantic mask or post-score rescue

research_basis.modflows: AAAI 2025 / arXiv:2503.19062 invertible RGB transport comparator
research_basis.classical_basis: one-dimensional monotone rearrangement is the exact empirical optimal transport for scalar gamut fraction
research_basis.position: clean-room explicit distributional baseline; no paper code, model, weights or novelty claim

stop_rules: Any fraction-transport invariant or automatic failure closes before visual preference.
Any severe or preference failure closes without changing rank, quantile interpolation or gates.
Pass opens only a wholly new source confirmation.
claim_ceiling: Development-only bounded monotone gamut-fraction transport evidence on consumed CC0 display proxies; not fresh confirmation, stock response, calibration, population preference or product promotion.
